type.pyramide.cfg.base_octaves.help: Generic octaves generated permanently, even with no consumer. With demand-driven auto-wiring, consumers request CUSTOM sizes → octaves are most often ORPHANED (wasted work and RAM bandwidth, which can make 50 fps interlaced sources BREAK when they sit at the edge of the budget). Default “None” (purely on demand). Only go back to Full/Minimal if a consumer really reads the octaves (e.g. generic monitoring).
type.pyramide.cfg.base_octaves.label: Always-generated octave base
Pyramid cores are sized to the load: cores = floor (6) + this ratio × Σ(source_resolution / 1080p), clamped to the node pool. Small = light node; large = dedicated multiview node. 0 = fixed cores (floor). Applied on (re)deployment (the cpuset cannot be changed while running).
SOFT threshold: every requested size is served up to the cap (6 per source). This threshold only arbitrates the surplus if there are MORE distinct sizes than the cap.
Custom-size threshold (only arbitrates beyond the size cap)
type.pyramide.cfg.log_level.help: Container log verbosity. Default “Events”: notable facts (start/stop, format change, reconnection, fallback to a degraded path, an input appearing or disappearing) are ALWAYS written — after a failure the log must let you reconstruct the story, and raising the level afterwards recovers nothing. Periodic metrics (fps, counters) are NOT logged: they are already published on :8080. “Verbose” = a flamethrower, one line per frame, to be enabled only for the duration of a diagnosis (the Docker log is not rotated).
type.pyramide.cfg.log_level.label: Log level
type.pyramide.cfg.n_inputs.label: Number of sources
type.pyramide.cfg.ring.label: Output ring (proxies)
type.pyramide.cfg.slice_lines.help: Band height (lines). Must divide the frame height (36 for 1080p) — otherwise falls back to whole frame.
type.pyramide.cfg.slice_lines.label: Lines per slice
type.pyramide.cfg.slice_mode.help: Reads the source band by band AND publishes the proxies the same way, so that downstream starts before the end of the frame. MEASURED on 2026-08-11: without this setting the pyramid read a sliced source and republished monolithic proxies — it cost the whole chain ONE full frame. Enabled, the stage delay of the consuming wall went from 3.0 to 1.0 frame. Interlaced source → falls back to whole frame.
type.pyramide.cfg.slice_mode.label: Slice mode (sub-frame latency)
